content: Neisseria gonorrhoeae, the bacterium responsible for gonorrhoea, can be transmitted from a pregnant woman to her newborn during delivery. This transmission can result in gonococcal ophthalmia neonatorum, a severe eye infection in the newborn, as well as systemic neonatal infections. In the mother, untreated gonorrhoea can lead to complications such as endometritis and pelvic sepsis. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the effectiveness of different antibiotic regimens in treating genital gonococcal infections during pregnancy, with a focus on reducing complications for both the mother and the newborn. The researchers conducted a search of the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register up to June 30, 2009, and later updated the search on January 3, 2012. No new trials were identified in the updated search. The review included randomized controlled trials that compared one antibiotic regimen to another in pregnant women with culture-confirmed gonococcal infections. Two trials, involving a total of 346 pregnant women, were included in the analysis. The primary outcome assessed in these trials was the rate of microbiological cure, determined by bacterial culture. The failure rates for achieving a microbiological cure were similar across the different antibiotic regimens tested. Specifically, the comparison of amoxicillin plus probenecid versus spectinomycin yielded a Peto odds ratio (Peto OR) of 2.29 (95% confidence interval (CI) 0.74 to 7.08). Similarly, the comparison of amoxicillin plus probenecid versus ceftriaxone also resulted in a Peto OR of 2.29 (95% CI 0.74 to 7.08). The comparison of ceftriaxone versus cefixime showed a Peto OR of 1.22 (95% CI 0.16 to 9.01). Across all regimens, side effects were rare. The authors concluded that the small number of participants in each comparison limited the ability of the trials to detect significant differences between the antibiotic regimens. However, for pregnant women allergic to penicillin, the findings provide some reassurance that ceftriaxone and spectinomycin appear to be similarly effective in achieving microbiological cure. It is noted that one citation in the awaiting classification section of the review may influence the conclusions once it is assessed.
